desc:
A grid describes a maze. A cell holds -1 for a wall, 0 for an ordinary open cell, or a positive number p for a portal cell. Every positive label appears on exactly two cells, and these two cells are twins.

You start in the top-left cell and want to reach the bottom-right cell. One step is either (a) a move to an adjacent cell (up, down, left, right) that is not a wall, or (b) if you are standing on a portal cell, a jump to its twin. Both kinds of step cost one. Return the minimum number of steps, or -1 if the goal cannot be reached.

grid = [[0, 1,-1, 0],
        [-1,-1,-1,-1],
        [0, 0, 1, 0]]

result = 3      ((0,0) -> (0,1) -> jump to (2,2) -> (2,3))

Portals can be walked through like open cells; stepping onto a portal does not move you automatically, it only gives you the option of a jump on the next step.
constraints: grid[r][c] is -1, 0, or a positive integer up to 1,000
Every positive label occurs exactly twice
The top-left and bottom-right cells are both 0
hints: Add the portal jumps as extra edges to the usual grid graph; all edges still cost one.
Before the search, scan the grid once and record, for every portal cell, the position of its twin.
BFS: from a cell, push the open 4-neighbours and, if the cell is a portal, also its twin. The first time the bottom-right cell is dequeued gives the answer.
editorial: Portals do not change the nature of the problem: each cell has up to four ordinary neighbours plus, for portal cells, one extra neighbour (the twin), and every edge costs one. The graph is still unweighted, so BFS is the right tool.

Preprocess with a dictionary from label to the first cell seen; when the second cell with the same label appears, store both as twins of each other. During BFS, expand each cell to its non-wall neighbours and its twin if it has one, marking cells visited when pushed.

The preprocessing and the search each touch every cell a constant number of times: O(rows × cols) time and space. A portal can be a shortcut across the whole maze, so a plain grid distance (Manhattan or even plain BFS) is not enough.
